definitions.explanation: For something to move downward due to gravity. The intransitive form—the object falls by itself.
To not pass an examination or test.

definitions.gloss: to come off, to be removed
definitions.explanation: For stains, dirt, or attachments to come off or be removed from a surface.

examples.japanese: {葉|は}っぱが{木|き}から{落|お}ちた。
examples.english: The leaves fell from the tree.
examples.notes: から marks the origin point of falling

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}に{落|お}ちてしまった。
examples.notes: に marks what you failed to get into; {落|お}ちる = fail (selection/application)

examples.japanese: {洗|あら}っても{汚|よご}れが{落|お}ちなくて{困|こま}った。
examples.english: The dirt wouldn't come off even after washing, so I was stuck.
examples.notes: {汚|よご}れが{落|お}ちる = dirt comes off

examples.japanese: {日|ひ}が{落|お}ちる{前|まえ}に{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}りたいと{思|おも}っているから、もう{行|い}こう。
examples.english: I want to get home before the sun sets, so let's go now.
examples.notes: {日|ひ}が{落|お}ちる = the sun sets

examples.japanese: {階段|かいだん}から{落|お}ちて{足|あし}を{怪我|けが}してしまったので、{今日|きょう}は{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}むことにした。
examples.english: I fell down the stairs and hurt my leg, so I decided to stay home from school today.

examples.japanese: {財布|さいふ}が{落|お}ちていますよ。
examples.english: Your wallet has fallen (is on the ground).

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちたらどうしよう。
examples.english: What should I do if I fail the exam?

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}に{落|お}ちてしまった。
examples.english: I failed to get into the university.

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}で{落|お}ちた{理由|りゆう}がわからない。
examples.english: I don't know why I failed the interview.

examples.japanese: {運転|うんてん}{免許|めんきょ}の{試験|しけん}に{三回|さんかい}{落|お}ちた。
examples.english: I failed the driver's license test three times.

examples.japanese: このシミは{なかなか|なかなか}{落|お}ちない。
examples.english: This stain won't come off easily.

examples.japanese: {化粧|けしょう}が{落|お}ちてしまった。
{油汚|あぶらよご}れはお{湯|ゆ}で{落|お}ちやすい。
examples.english: Oil stains come off easily with hot water.

examples.japanese: ボタンが{落|お}ちそうだ。
examples.english: The button looks like it's about to fall off.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pair: {落|お}とす (transitive, to drop something). Pattern: Xが{落|お}ちる (X falls).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {落|お}ちている = 'has fallen' (is lying on the ground) or 'is off' (for stains).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{木|き}から{落|お}ちる (fall from a tree)
・{床|ゆか}に{落|お}ちる (fall onto the floor)
・{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちる (fail an exam)
・{汚|よご}れが{落|お}ちる (dirt comes off)
・{雷|かみなり}が{落|お}ちる (lightning strikes—lit. 'falls')
・{日|ひ}が{落|お}ちる (the sun sets)

NOTE ON KANJI: The vocabulary list shows {落|お}る but the standard form is {落|お}ちる with the ち included.

IDIOMS:
・{落|お}ち{着|つ}く (to calm down—compound verb)
・{気|き}が{落|お}ちる (to feel down)

REGISTER: Neutral.
